classification.difficultyReason: Calculate each sector's arc as a fraction of its circle's circumference, then add both radii.

content.prompt:
Use $\pi\approx3.14$ to find the approximate value of the perimeter of the sector with:

Give answers to 2 decimal places.

children.label: a
children.prompt: radius $10$ m, containing an angle of $30^\circ$

answer.worked:
The arc is $\frac{30}{360}$ of the full circumference. Add the two radii.

$$\begin{align*}P&=\frac{30}{360}\times2\pi\times10+2\times10\\P&=\frac{5\pi}{3}+20\\P&\approx\frac{5\times3.14}{3}+20\\P&\approx25.23\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: radius $9$ cm, containing an angle of $10^\circ$

answer.worked:
The arc is $\frac{10}{360}$ of the full circumference. Add the two radii.

$$\begin{align*}P&=\frac{10}{360}\times2\pi\times9+2\times9\\P&=\frac{\pi}{2}+18\\P&\approx\frac{3.14}{2}+18\\P&\approx19.57\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: radius $24$ m, containing an angle of $135^\circ$

spec.description: Unshaded 135-degree sector with centre O, a horizontal radius extending right labelled 24 m, and a radius extending upper-left. Ordinary source blue outlines and red centre marker are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Both straight sides are radii of length 24 m; the included central angle is 135 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and labels are permanent question givens; no answer is shown.

answer.worked:
The arc is $\frac{135}{360}$ of the full circumference. Add the two radii.

$$\begin{align*}P&=\frac{135}{360}\times2\pi\times24+2\times24\\P&=18\pi+48\\P&\approx18\times3.14+48\\P&\approx104.52\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
